newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT -JGBs seen stuck near recent ranges.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -JGBs seen stuck near recent ranges.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures are expected to be range-bound on Tuesday, with the upside capped by yen weakness versus the dollar and recent firmness in Tokyo share prices, traders said.
"I think the yen's recent weakness against the dollar will make JGBs heavy on the upside...but I don't expect JGBs to fall sharply," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.

The yen's decline against the dollar is of some concern, but as long as the yen lingers near present levels there is likely to be relatively little impact on JGBs, said a trader for another city bank's securities affiliate.
There may be some hedge selling related to a four-year JGB auction expected during the day, the second trader said.

"Without Nomura (Securities), there is some concern that the market may have some difficulty absorbing JGBs with maturities of four to six years, and such worries may invite hedge selling of JGB futures," the trader said.

Nomura Securities has been suspended from JGB auctions and underwriting since May, after the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission filed complaints against prosecutors alleging that Nomura and three of its former executives had illegally compensated a corporate client for losses.
Traders said that the coupon rate for the new four-year issue is likely to be set at 1.3 percent and that the volume offered is likely to be 400 billion yen.
"There should be some investor demand for the four-year notes, as some investors have shown a preferance for medium-term bonds over bonds with longer maturities," the first trader said.
